title: Cross-Function Reentrancy
summary: A bank guards withdraw() with a reentrancy lock — but leaves transfer() unguarded. During withdraw()'s external call you cannot re-enter withdraw, but you CAN call transfer() to move your not-yet-zeroed balance to an accomplice.
web2Analog: Inconsistent locking: one critical section is synchronized but a sibling that touches the same state is not — a partial mutex that a determined caller routes around.

identify.question: Why does the reentrancy guard fail to stop the attack?
options: withdraw() is missing the noReentrant modifier
transfer() has no guard and is reachable during withdraw()'s callback, so the not-yet-zeroed balance can be moved
identify.explanation: The lock only protects withdraw(). During withdraw()'s external call the attacker's balance is still set, and transfer() (unguarded) can move that balance to a second account, which then withdraws it separately. Reentrancy guards must cover every function that touches the shared state.

hints: withdraw() IS guarded — so re-entering withdraw() directly will revert. What else touches balanceOf?
During the callback your balance hasn't been zeroed yet. Is there an unguarded function that lets you move it?
From receive(), call transfer() to push your balance to a helper contract, then withdraw it from there.
The fix: apply the reentrancy guard to transfer() too, or follow checks-effects-interactions in withdraw().
